note: Rewritten from Emerson (1959); the description of the holotype soldier, the measurement table (table 7), the locality and the depository of the type material are omitted; the worker is not described.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Compared with paratype soldiers of D. furcatidens, colour and pilosity similar, body smaller. Head with a deeper depression above and behind the antennal bases, and a weaker elevation above the base of the mandibles. Posterior part of the postmentum straighter, the transition to the convex anterior part less abrupt than in the latter; posterior part without a transverse ridge or groove, but narrowing more pronounced and anterior part more swollen. Antennae 13-segmented, segment 3 apparently formed by the fusion of two segments and slightly longer than segment 2, segment 4 shorter than segment 2, the fifth segment equal to or slightly shorter than segment 2. Mandibles shorter but much resembling those of D. furcatidens. Anterior margin of the pronotum with a blunter notch, angles slightly larger than a right angle. Fore coxa with a more distinct flattened area inside the sharp ridge, bearing several conspicuous dark setae. Outer margin of the middle tibia without conspicuous spines; tibial spurs 3:2:2, the outer spur of the fore tibia extremely reduced, almost invisible. The other 7 soldiers from the same nest agree with the description of the holotype; only 1 has one antenna similar to that described for D. furcatidens.
